# Change-control checklist — platform facilities

Applies to every change raised against the facility estate, including work carried out by vendors under
a framework agreement. The checklist is filled in by the change raiser and countersigned by the shift
supervisor before the ticket leaves draft.

## Before the change

- [ ] A change record exists with a single named owner, a start and end window, and a rollback step written
      by someone other than the person who will execute it.
- [ ] The rollback step names the exact state to restore and the person who verifies it afterwards.
- [ ] Any safety interlock that must be bypassed is listed, together with the mitigation that replaces it
      while the bypass is active.
- [ ] The affected room and rack are named. "Facilities" is not an acceptable location.
- [ ] A second engineer has read the plan and signed it. For changes that touch power distribution the
      reviewer must be from the electrical team.

## During the change

## Structure of a note

The first paragraph says what customers can observe, in their terms. The second says what is being done and
by whom. The third, when known, says when the next update will follow. Anything else — hypotheses, internal
tooling names, the names of engineers — is left out of the customer-facing note and recorded in the internal
timeline instead.

Internal notes carry more detail. They name the working theory, the person testing it, and the two or three
diagnostics already excluded. An internal note that lists every alarm without saying which ones were ruled
out costs the next responder the same investigation twice.

## Postmortem

A postmortem is written for every S1 and for any S2 that repeated within the quarter. It is blameless in the
narrow sense that it names systems and decisions rather than individuals, and it ends with no more than
three actions, each with an owner and a date. Postmortems with ten actions are treated as having none: the
review samples whether the actions were completed, and a list nobody finishes scores worse than a short one
that closes.

## Escalation touchpoints

Handovers are written, not spoken. A spoken handover reaches the next shift and nobody else; a written one
reaches the engineer who is called at three in the morning two weeks later and needs to know why a circuit
was left isolated.

## Standing notes

The plant rooms are visited on a walking round twice per shift. Round times are recorded, because a round
that is consistently recorded at the same minute is a round that is being signed off from the office. The
security lead samples the timestamps monthly and has, on two occasions, asked for the round to be repeated
under observation.

Rooms under construction are excluded from the round only while the contractor's permit is open, and the
exclusion ends automatically when the permit expires. An exclusion that outlives its permit is treated as a
finding in the next audit.

## Out of hours

# Export reading guide — riser assembly extracts

## Why this guide exists

The assembly exports are written by a field extractor that puts one record per line and omits the header
row. The omission is deliberate: the extractor is shared by four teams, and a header written by one team
would be wrong for the others. The order for each family is therefore recorded here and nowhere else, and
every extract names its family on its first line.

## Field order by family

| Extract family | Field order |
|---|---|
| third-riser assembly | asset identifier, certified value, test pressure, verification date |
| north-riser assembly | asset identifier, test pressure, certified value, verification date |
| low-voltage distribution | asset identifier, certified value, verification date |
| roof plant | asset identifier, test pressure, verification date |

The two riser families share a shape but not an order. A record copied from one family into a ticket for
the other parses cleanly and reads wrongly, which is why the family name is printed on the first line of
every extract and why this table is the only place the order is written down.

# Third-riser assembly export

Extract of the valve records for the third riser, one record per line. The extractor that produced
this file omits the header row; the order of the fields is defined in the export reading guide, and a
line that does not carry four fields is a malformed extract rather than a valve with missing data.

Records are ordered by identifier. Dates are the day the reading was verified, not the day the
valve was installed.

# North-riser assembly export

Extract of the valve records for the north riser, one record per line, produced by the same extractor as
the other riser exports and therefore also without a header row. The field order for this family of
exports is defined in the export reading guide and is not the same for every riser.

Records are ordered by identifier. A line that does not carry four fields is a malformed extract.

- **Change-control checklist — platform facilities**: pre-change requirements (named owner, window, independent rollback step, interlock bypass mitigations, named room/rack, second-engineer sign-off with electrical-team reviewer for power distribution changes).
- **Structure of a note**: customer-facing note format (observable impact → what's being done and by whom → next update), internal notes with working theory and ruled-out diagnostics, postmortem rules (S1 and repeat S2, blameless, max three actions with owner and date), written handovers, standing notes on walking rounds and construction exclusions, and an "Out of hours" heading.
- **Export reading guide — riser assembly extracts**: headerless, one record per line, family named on the first line, with field orders for third-riser, north-riser, low-voltage distribution, and roof plant families, plus the warning that the two riser families share a shape but not an order.

## Field notes

The certified value is the rating recorded when the assembly is certified and revised only by the
certifying team. The test pressure is a single measurement taken during the pressure test and is not
maintained afterwards. The verification date is the day the reading was checked, not the day the assembly
was installed.

## Corrections

A change to a field order is a new release of this guide and is announced to all four teams together. The
guide is not released per family: one release covers every family, so a family cannot be reading an order
that another family has already changed.
